root_idea.summary: The root centers on bringing something into appearance: showing, indicating, and becoming manifest rather than remaining concealed.
root_idea.development: Its lexical development extends from an affair becoming overt, to making an affair known or public, mutual open disclosure, and عَلَانِيَةٌ as openness opposed to secrecy.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The supplied group is a Quran-attested Form IV verb with an appropriate classical perfect-tense citation form.
The supplied group is a Quran-attested nominal with an independently established dictionary headword.

senses.definition: To lay an affair open; to reveal, declare, or publish it.
senses.usage_conditions: An active Form IV verb for making something known or public, especially an affair, statement, or information; it contrasts in Quranic usage with concealing or keeping something secret.

senses.definition: Openness or publicity; openly, publicly, and in some adverbial contexts aloud.
senses.usage_conditions: A noun used adverbially, especially in contrast with secrecy; the supplied Quranic occurrences express doing something openly or publicly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An affair, case, or event became overt, manifest, open, or public.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form I use said of an affair, case, or event.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mutual openness: acting openly with another, openly showing hostility, or mutually laying open what is in one's mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal construction involving open dealing or mutual disclosure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reveal or confess an enormity, specifically an act of adultery.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported specialized use of the Form IV verb, applied to a person accused of adultery; the gender of the reported subject is not a general lexical restriction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a person publicly known.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction with بِـ in which the person is brought into public notice; the source presents this as an additional reported use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An affair, case, or event became notorious or commonly known.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form IV construction, equivalent to becoming publicly known.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek publicity, either by seeking to be made publicly known or by desiring to make something public.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form X expressing pursuit or desire of public disclosure or public notice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give a title to a book or other writing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare specialized Form Q.Q use applied to titling written material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who reveals secrets or does not conceal a secret.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A personal noun describing habitual disclosure of secrets; the source's example does not restrict the meaning to men.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One's outward aspect or external self.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive use opposed to the inner or concealed self.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person whose affair or case is open or manifest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use describing a person characterized by public visibility.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The title of a book or other writing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal term for the heading or title of written material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Overt, open, manifest, public, published, or spread.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participle applied to an affair, case, or event.
